key_insight: Generalist and foundation models were tested against dermatology-specific classifiers, and the study finds that performance still drops under real-world shifts in image type, device quality, and patient diversity.
clinical_relevance: The work highlights why skin-lesion AI must be evaluated across dermoscopy and smartphone photos before it can be considered reliable for clinical use.
method: Benchmarked recent models on dermatology datasets.
Compared general-purpose, medical vision-language, foundation, and task-specific classifiers.
Evaluated robustness under modality shifts, distribution changes, and demographic variability.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes benchmarking across recent dermoscopic and smartphone-based datasets, with evaluation focused on performance under distribution shift, modality change, and demographic variability.
watch_item: Results from curated datasets may not fully predict performance in local clinics, especially where imaging protocols and patient populations differ.
paper_title: Bridging Research and Practice: A Systematic Evaluation of Generalist and Dermatology-Specific Models in Clinical Skin Lesion Classification
